sections.title: Adding symbols
content: Click any arrow (connector) in the flowchart: a symbol picker opens, and the symbol you pick is inserted there.
The new symbol opens for editing right away. In every popup, Enter presses the default (blue) button, e.g. Save or OK; Esc closes the popup.

sections.title: Editing and deleting
content: Click a symbol to edit it. Use the Delete button in its editor to remove it.

sections.title: Right mouse button: cut and paste
content: Right-click a symbol to cut it (an If or loop moves together with everything inside it). A badge in the header shows what was cut.
Right-click an arrow to paste it there. With nothing cut, the symbol picker opens instead.
Click the badge in the header to discard the cut symbol (it is then lost).

sections.title: Procedures and functions
content: Use the "+ Routine" tab to create a procedure or function with parameters; edit it with the ✎ icon. Call it with a Call symbol or from an expression, e.g. Double(n).
A function's return value is the value of the variable named after the function when it ends. A parameter marked "by reference" changes the caller's variable; arrays are always passed by reference.

sections.title: Structs (records)
content: Use "+ Struct" to create your own type with a name and fields (e.g. Point: x, y). A field can be of a basic type or another struct. Click a struct's tab to edit, rename or delete it.

A struct can be chosen anywhere a type is: in Declare (also as an array), for parameters and as a function's return type. Access fields with a dot: p.x, t[i].name, r.corner.x — in expressions, assignments and Input.
Assignment (b = a) and by-value parameters copy the struct; a by-reference parameter changes the original.

sections.title: Files
content: On the Files tab you can upload files, create new ones, view and edit their content, rename, download and delete them. Files are kept in this browser.
A program refers to a file by its name, as a String: "file-a". Symbols: Open File (for reading, writing or appending), Read from File (reads one line into a variable), Write to File, Close File.

eof("file-a") is true when a file open for reading has no more lines — e.g. a loop: while not eof("file-a"). Read, Write, Close and EOF() may leave the file name out: then they use the most recently opened file (the way Flowgorithm handles files).
Opening a file for writing creates (or overwrites) it; what the program creates appears on the Files tab right away, ready to download.

sections.title: Running
content: ▶ Run executes the program; the symbol being executed is highlighted in blue. Set the pace with the Speed selector.
⏸ Pause stops the run; continue with ▶ or ⏭.
⟲ Reset starts over and clears the console and variables.
An Input symbol asks for a value on the Console tab; the program waits until you enter it.

sections.title: Stepping
content: The ⏭ Step button executes one symbol at a time. Follow the current variable values on the Variables tab and the output on the Console tab. You can switch to ▶ Run at any time.

sections.title: Debugging
content: Breakpoint: Shift + click a symbol, or tick "Breakpoint" in its editor. A red dot in the corner of the symbol marks it.
When running, the program stops at a breakpoint before executing that symbol, and switches to the Variables tab.
Variables changed by the last step are highlighted in yellow.
Continue step by step (⏭) or to the next breakpoint (▶).
Breakpoint symbol (as in Flowgorithm): the run stops when it gets there — with a condition (e.g. i = 4), only when the condition is true.
On a runtime error, the symbol that caused it is highlighted and the message appears in the console.

sections.title: Expressions
content: Arrays: t[i], indexed from 0. Struct fields: p.x, t[i].name.
Strings in quotes: "apple" or 'apple' (no escape sequences; \ is an ordinary character).
Names (variables, routines) start with a letter and contain letters and digits; case doesn't matter.
The full list of operators and functions is in the tables below.

sections.title: View
content: Use the bottom-right controls to zoom in (+), zoom out (−) or fit the whole diagram (⛶). Drag the empty background to scroll. Drag the divider between the diagram and the side panel to set the panel width — this browser remembers it. Popups can be moved by dragging their title (or any empty part of them).

sections.title: Files, examples, source code
content: The Files tab manages the data files programs read and write (see Files).
Save: to a .flow file. Open: a .flow file, or a .fprg file made with Flowgorithm (anything the app doesn't support, e.g. turtle graphics, is reported). Your program is also kept in this browser.
Updates: when a new version of the app comes out, the page updates itself as soon as no program is running and no dialog is open — the open program and the view are kept.
The buttons in the header are icon-only (New, Open, Save, Export Image, then the run controls): hover over one to see which is which. Export Image makes a PNG image of the flowchart.
New: the window shown at start — an empty project or ready-made examples (algorithms, structs, files); a loaded example can be edited and continued as if you had written it.
The Code tab generates Python, C++ or C# source code from the program — highlighted, with line numbers; Enlarge shows it in a big window.

Pseudocode writes the program in the app's language: in English, the pseudocode of Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science (DECLARE, IF … THEN … ENDIF, FOR … NEXT, PROCEDURE, FUNCTION … RETURNS); in Hungarian, the mondatszerű leírás taught at ELTE. Arrays and strings are indexed from 0 here too, as in the flowchart.

appImage.label: Linux · AppImage
appImage.note: no installation, any distribution: make it executable (chmod +x), then run it

deb.label: Linux · .deb package
deb.note: Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint: sudo apt install ./{file}

exe.label: Windows · .exe installer
exe.note: Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit); if SmartScreen warns: More info, then Run anyway

msi.label: Windows · .msi package
msi.note: for school machines and administrators: silent or central install, e.g. msiexec /i {file} /qn
